Compare cross-validated models

Source: R/crossval.R
compare_cv.Rd

Compares models cross-validated on the same cells with the same folds (the same folds and seed in crossval()). The log scores are compared cell by cell, which removes most of the variation between cells: the difference from the best model is given with its standard error, the standard deviation of the per-cell differences over the square root of the number of cells. A difference of less than about two standard errors is not a clear preference.

Usage

compare_cv(...)

Arguments

...

Two or more stareal_cv objects, named (e.g. compare_cv(default = cv1, no_nugget = cv2)); unnamed ones are named by their expressions.

Value

A data frame, one row per model, best first: model, n_cells, mean_log_score, diff (from the best model), se_diff, pct_outside_95, rmse, correlation.

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- simulate_areal(areal_lattice(4, 4), time_frame(n_steps = 5), n_cells = 40, seed = 1)
ctl <- list(n_iter = 100, n_burn = 50, n_store = 25, n_chains = 1, ess_sweeps = 2, verbose = FALSE)
fit1 <- fit_areal(sim, control = ctl)
fit2 <- fit_areal(sim, nugget = FALSE, control = ctl)
compare_cv(nugget = crossval(fit1, folds = 4), no_nugget = crossval(fit2, folds = 4))
#>       model n_cells mean_log_score        diff    se_diff pct_outside_95
#> 1 no_nugget      40      -3.213514  0.00000000 0.00000000            5.0
#> 2    nugget      40      -3.254170 -0.04065535 0.03941771            2.5
#>       rmse correlation
#> 1 13.44538   0.5446642
#> 2 13.75298   0.5074830
# }
